elements.element: Customer owns deliverables/work product created for it
elements.evidence: 14.2 "Customer exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer."

elements.element: Vendor assigns its rights in deliverables to Customer
elements.evidence: "Vendor hereby irrevocably assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in each Deliverable."
14.3 "Vendor retains Vendor Technology." (defined as Vendor's pre-existing software, tools, templates)

elements.element: Perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to Vendor IP embedded in deliverables
elements.evidence: 13.2 "embedded in a Deliverable, Vendor grants Customer ... a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use ... modify"; 14.3 "the perpetual licence in Section 13.2 applies"

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data
elements.evidence: 14.1 "Customer owns all Customer Data ... No right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process that material solely to provide ... the Services"
14.4 "No jointly owned intellectual property is created unless the Parties sign a separate instrument"

elements.element: Vendor owns generic tools and know-how
elements.evidence: 14.3 "Vendor retains Vendor Technology."; Deliverable definition excludes "generally applicable ideas, methods, skills, and know-how"

elements.element: Customer licence to deliverables is perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free
elements.evidence: 14.2 as revised gives Customer ownership rather than a licence; the 13.2 perpetual licence covers "software and Vendor Technology", not Deliverables as such

elements.element: Customer may use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business
elements.evidence: 13.2 permits "modify, create derivative works from, and permit contractors to support" — no express sublicensing right, and it attaches to Vendor Technology

reasons: Preferred level is complete: ownership of Deliverables is vested in Customer, an express irrevocable Vendor assignment is added, Vendor's pre-existing Vendor Technology retention plus the perpetual/irrevocable/royalty-free embedded-IP licence in 13.2 survive, Customer Data ownership in 14.1 is untouched, and 14.4 continues to bar joint ownership absent a signed instrument.
Edits are confined to the two ownership/licence operators in 14.2 plus one short assignment sentence; no other sentence, exception, or commercial term was rewritten.

Fallback is not independently satisfied (no express perpetual worldwide licence to use, modify and sublicense Deliverables), but that is irrelevant because the drafter targeted and reached the preferred level; the two levels were not mixed.

Note only: reversing the second sentence of 14.2 leaves Vendor with a revocable, non-transferable, term-limited licence to use Deliverables it no longer owns. That does not contradict Customer ownership (Customer can revoke), but simply deleting the sentence would have been marginally cleaner.
No dangling references or undefined terms are introduced; 14.3's cross-reference to the Section 13.2 perpetual licence still operates.
